key_insight: Eddies reinforce western boundary currents along continental slopes, brake them at separation, and reinforce their free jets on the cyclonic flank, consistent with stabilized negative viscosity.
engineering_relevance: Ocean-flow models may better represent jet–eddy momentum exchange using a scale-stabilized closure that accommodates the sign reversal at coastal separation.
method: Measure cross-current eddy momentum fluxes in each current’s own frame using SWOT altimetry.
Test stabilized negative viscosity: a negative Laplacian term balanced by a positive biharmonic term.
Examine topographic constraints and evaluate the closure in an eddy-resolving reanalysis.
evidence_signal: Two years of SWOT data across five subtropical western boundary currents show slope viscosities near −10³ m²/s, braking at separation in all five, and cyclonic-flank free-jet viscosities near −10⁴ m²/s; reanalysis supports the SNV form across three basins.
watch_item: SWOT resolves the full SNV structure only in the Gulf Stream and Agulhas, so observational confirmation across all five currents remains incomplete.
paper_title: Stabilized negative viscosity governs ocean jets before, during and after they leave the coast
